extractedItems.title: Relief from wrong hole on a double green
extractedItems.question: Your ball lands on a double green, but the wrong hole is between your ball and the correct hole. What should you do?

choices.text: Play around the wrong hole as it lies.
Move your ball so the wrong hole is no longer in your way, without penalty.
Pick up the ball and start the hole again.
Ask your opponent to move their ball.

extractedItems.explanation: If the wrong hole is blocking your play, you can place your ball at the nearest point where it's no longer in your way, with no penalty.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A golfer on a big green with two holes, moving their ball sideways to avoid a hole that blocks their path to the flag.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Girl golfer on a double green, moving ball to avoid a wrong hole.

extractedItems.title: Conceding putts in stroke play
extractedItems.question: In stroke play, if a player picks up their ball before holing out, what must happen?

choices.text: They are allowed to record their last stroke and move on.
They must put the ball back with 1 penalty stroke and finish the hole.
They receive 2 penalty strokes automatically.
They must restart the hole.

extractedItems.explanation: If a player picks up their ball early in stroke play, they must put it back, add a penalty stroke, and finish the hole.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer picks up the ball next to the hole before finishing, looking confused.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Boy picking up golf ball before holing out.

extractedItems.title: Umbrellas and outside help while putting
extractedItems.question: During a putt, can another person hold an umbrella for a player to shield them from the rain?

choices.text: Yes, it is always allowed.
No, only the player can hold their own umbrella while playing.
Yes, but only if both players agree.
No, umbrellas are never allowed on the green.

extractedItems.explanation: You can't have someone else hold an umbrella for you while playing a stroke, but you can hold it yourself.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A girl golfer on the green preparing to putt, holding her own umbrella while it rains.

extractedItems.title: Practising after finishing a hole
extractedItems.question: You’ve finished the hole. Can you stay and practise putting or chipping on the green, and is there any place you can’t practise from?

choices.text: Yes, you can putt again for practice.
Yes, you can chip again for practice.
No, you can’t practise from a bunker.
Yes, you can practise from a bunker.

extractedItems.explanation: You may putt or chip again for practice unless it’s banned by Local Rules, but you can’t play practice shots from a bunker.

reviewedItems.title: Relief from wrong hole on a double green
reviewedItems.question: Your ball comes to rest on a double green, but the wrong hole is directly in the line between your ball and the correct hole. What are you allowed to do?

choices.text: Play your shot as it lies, even if the hole is in the way.
Take free relief by moving your ball sideways, no closer to the hole, so the wrong hole isn't in your way.
Pick up your ball and replay your last stroke.
Ask another player to cover the wrong hole.

reviewedItems.explanation: You're allowed free relief if the other hole interferes with your line. Place your ball at the nearest spot, not closer to the hole, where the wrong hole doesn't interfere.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer on a double green, placing his ball sideways away from a second hole that blocks his path to the flag.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Boy golfer on a double green, moving his ball away from the wrong hole.

reviewedItems.title: Conceding putts in stroke play
reviewedItems.question: In stroke play, what happens if a player picks up their ball before holing out, thinking their score is already made?

choices.text: Their score for the hole is finished as it stands.
They must replace the ball, add one penalty stroke, and finish the hole.
They get a two-stroke penalty but do not replay the shot.
They are disqualified from the competition.

reviewedItems.explanation: In stroke play, you must finish out the hole. If you pick up your ball before finishing, you need to put it back, add a penalty stroke, and finish the hole.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer on the green, looking uncertain as he picks up his ball before holing out.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Boy picking up golf ball before finishing the putt.

reviewedItems.title: Umbrellas and outside help while putting
reviewedItems.question: While you putt, can someone else hold an umbrella over you to protect you from rain?

choices.text: Yes, anyone can hold an umbrella for you while you play.
No, only you can hold your umbrella while playing a stroke.
Only your caddie can hold it for you.
Umbrellas aren't allowed on the course at all.

reviewedItems.explanation: Only the player is allowed to hold their umbrella during a stroke. Nobody else can shield you from the elements.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: Teenage boy golfer on the green, holding his own umbrella while preparing to putt in light rain.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Boy holding his own umbrella while putting.

reviewedItems.title: Practising after finishing a hole
reviewedItems.question: After finishing a hole, which types of practice are allowed on the green, and where are you not allowed to practise from?

choices.text: Practising extra putts on the green.
Practising extra chips on or just beside the green.
Playing practice shots from a bunker beside the green.
Practising putts or chips unless banned by Local Rules.

reviewedItems.explanation: You may practise extra putts or chips on or near the putting green after completing a hole, unless local rules ban it. You can't practise from a bunker.
